{{Short description|Behavioral ecologist and evolutionary biologist (1961–2021)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Barry R. Sinervo''' (1961–2021) was a behavioral ecologist and evolutionary biologist. He was a full professor at University of California Santa Cruz where his research interests included [[game theory]],<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Friedman|first1=Daniel|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vvhGCwAAQBAJ&q=barry+sinervo|title=Evolutionary Games in Natural, Social, and Virtual Worlds|last2=Sinervo|first2=Barry|date=2016|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-998115-1|language=en}}</ref> [[climate change]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sinervo|first1=Barry|last2=Méndez-de-la-Cruz|first2=Fausto|last3=Miles|first3=Donald B.|last4=Heulin|first4=Benoit|last5=Bastiaans|first5=Elizabeth|last6=Cruz|first6=Maricela Villagrán-Santa|last7=Lara-Resendiz|first7=Rafael|last8=Martínez-Méndez|first8=Norberto|last9=Calderón-Espinosa|first9=Martha Lucía|last10=Meza-Lázaro|first10=Rubi Nelsi|last11=Gadsden|first11=Héctor|date=2010-05-14|title=Erosion of Lizard Diversity by Climate Change and Altered Thermal Niches|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1184695|journal=Science|language=en|volume=328|issue=5980|pages=894–899|doi=10.1126/science.1184695|issn=0036-8075|pmid=20466932|bibcode=2010Sci...328..894S |hdl=10533/144943|s2cid=9578762|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Hepler|first=Lauren|date=2019-07-03|title=How Santa Cruz's Dr. Doom Beat Extinction Anxiety|url=https://goodtimes.sc/cover-stories/barry-sinervo-extinction/|access-date=2021-03-17|website=Good Times Santa Cruz|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Harvey|first=Chelsea|title=Warming Threatens Reptiles More Than Birds and Mammals|language=en|website=Scientific American|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/warming-threatens-reptiles-more-than-birds-and-mammals/|access-date=2021-03-17}}</ref> [[herpetology]], and animal behavior.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-13|title=Department Directory|url=https://www.eeb.ucsc.edu/about/dept-directory.php?uid=sinervo|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201213180152/https://www.eeb.ucsc.edu/about/dept-directory.php?uid=sinervo|archive-date=2020-12-13|access-date=2021-03-17|website=}}</ref> One of his major discoveries was of a [[Rock paper scissors|rock-paper-scissors]] game in [[side-blotched lizard]] mating behaviour.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Arnold|first=Carrie|title=Biodiversity May Thrive Through Games of Rock-Paper-Scissors|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/biodiversity-may-thrive-through-games-of-rock-paper-scissors-20200305/|access-date=2021-03-17|website=Quanta Magazine|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sinervo|first1=B.|last2=Lively|first2=C. M.|date=1996-03-21|title=The rock–paper–scissors game and the evolution of alternative male strategies|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/380240a0|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=380|issue=6571|pages=240–243|doi=10.1038/380240a0|bibcode=1996Natur.380..240S |s2cid=205026253|issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Ryerson|first=James|date=2007-12-09|title=Rock-Paper-Scissors Is Universal|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/12/09/magazine/09rockpaper.html|access-date=2021-03-17|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> He also discovered evidence of the [[Baldwin effect]] in the side-blotched lizard.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Knapton|first=Sarah|date=2018-09-06|title=How evolution can be super speedy when life depends on it|language=en-GB|work=The Telegraph|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/2018/09/06/evolution-can-super-speedy-life-depends/|access-date=2021-03-17|issn=0307-1235}}</ref> Sinervo was born in [[Port Arthur, Ontario]], Canada, and educated at [[Dalhousie University]], Nova Scotia, and the [[University of Washington]], Seattle. He died from cancer at age 60 on March 15, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stephens |first1=Tim |title=Influential evolutionary biologist Barry Sinervo dies at age 60 |url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2021/03/sinervo-in-memoriam.html |website=UC Santa Cruz News |language=en |date=March 22, 2021}}</ref>

== Honors ==
A species of lizard was named after Sinervo, ''[[Phymaturus sinervoi]]'' Scolaro et al., 2012.<ref>Scolaro, José A., Fausto R. Méndez-De La Cruz & Nora R. Ibargüengoytia. 2012. A new species of ''Phymaturus'' of the ''patagonicus'' clade (Squamata, Liolaemidae) from isolated plateau of southwestern Rio Negro Province, Argentina. Zootaxa 3451: 17-30.</ref>
